pr_title: Improve safety and logging of realm migration process
pr_body:
This PR creates point-in-time backups of both EF and realm databases before both beatmap and score migration operations. To recover / retry the migration, the user just needs to remove the filename suffix on both.

Also adds more logging to the migration process, and adds back the final `client.db` deletion after the migration completes.

- [x] Depends on #16428

I probably wouldn't recommend reviewing this until the dependency is merged.

![20220118 145128 (iTerm)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/149878670-fd165076-f813-46f3-b0e8-ab671ad6fa7c.png)

```csharp

[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:54 [verbose]: Beginning beatmaps migration to realm
[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:54 [verbose]: Found 99 beatmaps in EF
[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:54 [verbose]: Creating full EF database backup at client.before_beatmap_migration_1642485054.db
[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:54 [verbose]: Blocking realm operations.
[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:54 [verbose]: Creating full realm database backup at client.before_beatmap_migration_1642485054.realm
[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:54 [verbose]: Restoring realm operations.
[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:54 [verbose]: Successfully migrated 99 beatmaps to realm
[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:55 [verbose]: Beginning scores migration to realm
[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:55 [verbose]: No scores found to migrate
[database] 2022-01-18 05:50:55 [verbose]: Migration successful, deleting EF database

```

I did look at the potential of making a UI for this operation to give feedback, but it's not going to be a simple task (a lot of game-level components immediately start consuming realm on startup before we can show a UI). Going to wait to test against some large user databases before deciding if that's worth the effort of fixing.

Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/16441.
pr_comments:
A few other loose thoughts:

* I'm curious if there was a reason for taking snapshots of both realm and EF before score and beatmap migrations individually rather than just the one snapshot of both before everything?
* I've also [gone back to the discord discussion from earlier](https://discord.com/channels/188630481301012481/188630652340404224/932945257774071818) and having given it more thought I think that I still prefer the approach taken here (make backups, migrate everything, clean out EF). While I can see that leaving the old client db intact would be more convenient for both devs and users who want to downgrade, I'm worried that especially users may end up breaking their file store without even being aware about it due to going back and forth, and we'll have to keep chasing weird reports of databases being in weird states that should be otherwise impossible. To a degree I'm still expecting there to be issues, but with the current method at least I'd expect them to be loud and very distinctive.
 
  I could however agree with [leaving the old EF database intact on debug builds](https://discord.com/channels/188630481301012481/188630652340404224/932947201922052096) as a compromise. Not sure what @smoogipoo's thoughts on that are (and it kind of works for us because we're here every day, but may not work for occasional contributors).

> * I'm curious if there was a reason for taking snapshots of both realm and EF before score and beatmap migrations individually rather than just the one snapshot of both before everything?

The rationale was that one could silently fail and it could help in debugging, but that's probably not good enough reason. It made more sense when deletions were happening in EF per row/migration. One backup should be enough now.

I've added a notification that shows up only for debug builds to potentially ease concerns.

![20220119 103303 (osu!)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/150046818-71c39164-ac96-44a0-9cfc-21fdb3234975.png)

issue_context.title: Add recovery support when realm cannot be opened
issue_context.body:
Currently if a realm file can't be opened (usually due to backwards migration), the game will not start.

Instead, the game should create a fresh realm file and allow itself to start, along with letting the user know what happened so they can report the issue if it was unexpected.

Marking as p0 since I'd want to get this ready before a release happens with #16428.
comments: I'll suggest it here as to not pollute the already-way-too-huge migration PR thread, but I'd also consider backing up users' databases before the beatmap/score migration is performed itself to avoid irrecoverable data loss and allow people to rollback if post-migration realm doesn't work in some respect.

> I'll suggest it here as to not pollute the already-way-too-huge migration PR thread, but I'd also consider backing up users' databases before the beatmap/score migration is performed itself to avoid irrecoverable data loss and allow people to rollback if post-migration realm doesn't work in some respect.

Perhaps rather than nuking the old content, we can add a table + flag to the database to indicate migration completed? I have bad experiences with backing up user data from stable as there's always some way it goes wrong.
Definitely think this is required though.

If migration fails, it will throw before the old rows are deleted. Is there a scenario where that is not enough? Or are you trolling to allow users to roll back to an old version without manual backup?

I'm also worried about cases where the migration may be accidentally aborted or the resulting database may not be usable due to some other performance concerns. I have worries that may happen for users with large beatmap collections.

review_comments: The `context != null` check is to just make calling the migration from `OsuGameBase.load()` work, correct? Maybe it should be marked with a removal TODO at some point when it's no longer required?
I'm not sure there will be a point it's not required. I think we want to be able to freely use realm during the initial load? Not sure.
I suppose there shouldn't be much of an issue with that, yeah.
